newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila opponents gather for banned Kinshasa march.
newsitem.headline: Kabila opponents gather for banned Kinshasa march.

text.p: Groups of opposition militants gathered in central Kinshasa on Wednesday for a banned protest march against self-proclaimed president Laurent Kabila and his new government.
Small groups of soldiers from Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo maintained a discreet watch on events at the Central Station, rallying point for the protest.
"We are marching to protest about the Rwandans they have put in the government," Jean-Claude Mukendi, an unemployed youth and supporter of veteran opposition leader Etienne Tshiekedi, told Reuters.
"Mr Tshisekedi knows the Zairean people do not want to be ruled by foreigners."

Opposition activists say that Tshisekedi was the constitutionally elected prime minister in the former Zaire, which Kabila has renamed the Democratic Republic of Congo, and should be allowed to take office as such.
They say certain ministers in Kabila's new 13 member government are Rwandans and denounce the presence of soldiers from Rwanda and other neighbouring states among his forces patrolling the capital.
Kinshasa newspapers dished up a mixed bag of headlines with the independent Reference Plus predicting a showdown between Tshisekedi's party and Kabila's Alliance on Wednesday.

Palmares, close to the opposition, headlined U.S. pressure on Kabila to broaden his government while Le Soft, whose proprietor was ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko's last information minister, spoke of a "totalitariatian lurch" under Kabila.
